To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are no significant differences in immunohistochemical expression of plakoglobin, desmoplakine, or connexin- 43 in ARVC when compared to controls.
immunohistochemically stained sections of heart tissue from patients with ARVC showed a similar expression of junctional plaque proteins as compared to control subjects.

immunohistochemically stained sections of the heart from patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricle cardiomyopathy show a small and insignificant decrease of expression of junctional protein compared to controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of cardiac arrhythmia.
the use of immunohistochemistry to detect desmosomal proteins and connexin- 43 in patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricle cardiomyopathy (ARC) and in control hearts.
a new diagnostic method of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of desmosomal proteins in ARVC is not different than in control hearts and is not useful in the diagnosis of ARVC.
the expression of desmosomal and connexin-3 protein is not significantly decreased in ARVC.
immunohistochemically detected desmosome protein expression is not useful for diagnosis of ARVC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of desmosomal junction proteins in the myocardium of ARVC patients is not decreased.
the immunohistochemical expression of junctional proteins does not differ between control subjects and ARVC patients.
there is no difference in the expression of these proteins between the diseased and control hearts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunohistochemstry is not a useful method of diagnosing ARVC.
immunohistochemically detectable desmosomal protein expression is preserved even when there is a genetic defect.
the diagnosis of ARVC should be made by a combination of clinical, genetic, histologic, and imaging data.
